claim: Manusmriti has a recoverable textual tradition with manuscript variation
The surviving Manusmriti manuscript tradition contains multiple textual readings
Some manuscripts contain additional verses not accepted in the critical text
The initial invocatory verse before verse 1 is absent from the Southern manuscript tradition
The initial invocatory verse is present in 18 northern manuscripts
Govinda comments on the initial invocatory verse
Olivelle nevertheless classifies the initial invocatory verse as spurious
Kulluka's recension became highly influential in later printed editions
William Jones explicitly based his translation on the text/gloss associated with Kulluka
Buhler's textual methodology differs materially from Jones's
Some differences between modern quotations of Manusmriti and the critical text may originate in recension, transmission, editorial or translation history
A controversial passage cannot be classified as an interpolation solely because of its subject matter
